chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When a martyr dies on the day of his death or the next day, he is buried in his clothes; and if he remains for some days until his wound changes, he is washed."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified in the Book of Salat that reliance is placed on the narration that states: if he dies in the battle, he is not washed; and if he is carried from it while still alive and then dies, at any time, washing is obligatory in all cases. This narration is weak, its chain consists of the men of the Zaydiyyah, and it is permissible that it emerged as a form of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing a martyr before burial if they survive the initial battle?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a martyr who dies instantly on the battlefield, who is buried unwashed in their garments, and one who survives long enough to be ritually washed. The commentator, likely Shaykh al-Tusi or his source, critiques the weak chain of the 'unwashed' rule, suggesting it may stem from *taqiyyah* (concealment), thereby reinforcing the general principle that martyrs undergo *ghusl* unless death is immediate. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of weighing chain reliability against practical ritual application.
